uncited: AR-NeRF builds on the [Scene Representation and Architecture](11368-scene-representation-and-architecture.md) principles, specifically the use of coupled MLPs for density and color prediction, but modifies the ray generation and training loop to support aperture rendering.
One ray origin is placed at the center of the aperture.
*   **Aperture Size Range:** The aperture size $s$ is sampled from a half-normal distribution.
*   **Time Complexity:** Rendering time is proportional to the number of rays per pixel.

Unlike standard NeRF, which assumes a pinhole camera, AR-NeRF represents each pixel using a collection of rays converging at a focus plane, allowing the model to disentangle defocus-aware and defocus-independent representations through aperture randomized training [S1].

The claim is fully supported by the evidence in Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that 'in contrast to the standard NeRF, which represents each pixel using a single ray under the pinhole camera assumption, AR-NeRF employs an aperture camera... that represents each pixel using a collection of rays that converge at the focus plane.' It further confirms that 'to disentangle defocus-aware and defocus-independent representations in an unsupervised manner, we introduce aperture randomized training, in which we learn to generate images in a GAN framework while changing the aperture size and latent codes both randomly and independently.'
